name: Give an example of science in everyday life
description: Student can give an example of how people use science in everyday life. [AS clause A]
exampleOfSuccess: The student says people use science to know which materials keep us warm, or to make and control sounds in music.
commonError: Student thinks science only happens in a laboratory or at school, not in everyday activities.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to name one way people use science in everyday life and explain it briefly.
reviewNotes: Confidence high. Serves AS-04 clause A.

name: Describe using a pattern to predict
description: Student can describe how people use a pattern they have noticed to predict what will happen, using a real example such as the Moon's phases or the Sun's daily path. [AS clause B]
exampleOfSuccess: The student explains that because the Moon's shape changes in the same order each month, people can predict when the next full Moon will be.
commonError: Student describes the pattern but not the prediction it allows, or treats the prediction as a lucky guess rather than based on the pattern.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to give one example of a pattern and what people can predict from it.
reviewNotes: Confidence high. Serves AS-04 clause B. CROSS-DESCRIPTOR CANDIDATE with AC9S2U01 IC8.

name: Describe how a worker uses science knowledge
description: Student can describe how someone in a job or activity uses what they know about science, such as a musician using patterns of sound or a woodworker knowing about the properties of materials. [AS clause A]
exampleOfSuccess: The student explains that a musician arranges sounds in patterns to make music, or that a woodworker chooses a material because it bends or is strong.
commonError: Student describes what the worker makes without saying what science knowledge they use.
checkpointTask: Name a worker (musician, woodworker, product designer). Ask the student what science they use in their work.

name: Describe using science to solve an everyday problem
description: Student can describe how people use science to solve an everyday problem, such as managing sound so as not to disturb others, or physically changing materials to reuse them and reduce waste. [AS clause A]
exampleOfSuccess: The student explains that using headphones or closing a door softly manages sound, or that changing materials lets us reuse them instead of throwing them away.
commonError: Student names the problem but not the science-based way people manage it.
checkpointTask: Pose an everyday situation (noise at home, too much waste). Ask the student how people use science to help.

name: Describe First Nations use of sky patterns
description: Student can describe an example of how First Nations Australians use patterns in the sky to predict events or to navigate. [AS clause B]
exampleOfSuccess: The student describes how the appearance of a particular star pattern signals a season, or helps with finding direction at night.
commonError: Student retells a story without identifying the sky pattern or the prediction or navigation it supports.
checkpointTask: After sharing a First Nations account, ask the student what sky pattern is used and what it helps people know or do.
reviewNotes: Confidence medium-high. From elaborations 1 and 9. RECOMMEND a First Nations authored or endorsed source.

name: Describe how a smart device uses patterns
description: Student can describe how a voice- or sound-activated tool uses patterns to help people in daily life. [AS clauses A and B]
exampleOfSuccess: The student explains that a voice assistant listens for the pattern of a person's voice or words to turn on a light or answer a question.
commonError: Student describes what the device does without mentioning that it responds to a sound or voice pattern.
checkpointTask: Ask the student how a voice-activated device knows what to do, and how it helps someone.
